passages.text: Page Overview 72 Results of Operations by Registrant 73 Sempra 73 SDG&E 83 SoCalGas 86 Capital Resources and Liquidity 88 Critical Accounting Estimates 108 New Accounting Standards 112 OVERVIEW This combined MD&A includes the operational and financial results of the following three Registrants: ▪ Sempra is a holding company whose principal businesses are regulated utilities in California and Texas. Our businesses invest in and operate electric and gas utilities and other energy infrastructure that provide energy services to customers. ▪ SDG&E is a regulated public utility that provides electric service to San Diego and southern Orange counties and natural gas service to San Diego County. ▪ SoCalGas is a regulated public natural gas distribution utility, serving customers throughout most of Southern California and part of central California. Sempra has the following three reportable segments which reflect how the CODM oversees operational and financial performance: ▪ Sempra California ▪ Sempra Texas Utilities ▪ Sempra Infrastructure SDG&E and SoCalGas each have one reportable segment. Below are significant events, including major project updates, that affected our business in 2025 and may continue to affect our future results: ▪ The 2025 Wildfire Legislation was signed into law and established, among other things, an $18 billion Continuation Account that would provide additional liquidity to reimburse catastrophic wildfire-related claims incurred by large California electric IOUs if the Wildfire Fund is depleted, and a multi-stakeholder task force, coordinated by the Wildfire Fund’s administrator, to prepare and submit to the California legislature and Governor of California on or before April 1, 2026, a report that evaluates and sets forth recommendations on new models to complement or replace the Wildfire Fund ▪ The CPUC issued an FD for SDG&E’s and SoCalGas’ cost of capital for 2026 through 2028 ▪ The CPUC issued an FD in SDG&E’s 2024 GRC Track 2 request that authorizes partial recovery of SDG&E’s WMP costs ▪ Oncor filed its 2025 comprehensive base rate review and expects to receive a final order from the PUCT in the first half of 2026 ▪ In June 2025, Texas House Bill 5247, which established the UTM, was signed into law and became effective ▪ In September 2025, we entered into an agreement to sell 45% of our equity interest in SI Partners to the KKR Partners for an aggregate base purchase price of approximately $9.99 billion, subject to adjustments, and expect the sale to close in the second or third quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions ▪ In December 2025, we entered into an agreement to sell Ecogas for 9.0 billion Mexican pesos (approximately $500 million U.S. dollar-equivalent at December 31, 2025), subject to adjustments, and expect the sale to close in the second or third quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions ▪ We sold a 49.9% equity interest in the PA LNG Phase 2 project to Blackstone ▪ SI Partners reached a positive FID on the PA LNG Phase 2 project and issued a full notice-to-proceed under Bechtel’s fixed-price EPC contract ▪ We invested $12.6 billion in capital expenditures and investments 2025 Form 10-K | 72 Tab

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: When evaluating our company and its businesses and any investment in our or their securities, you should carefully consider the following risk factors and all other information contained in this report and the other documents we file with the SEC (including those filed subsequent to this report). We also may be materially harmed by risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently consider immaterial. If any of these risks occur, our results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and/or prospects could be materially adversely affected, our actual results could differ materially from those expressed or implied in our forward-looking statements, and the trading prices of our securities and those of our businesses could decline. These risk factors are not prioritized in order of importance or materiality, and they should be read together with the other information in this report, including in the Consolidated Financial Statements and in “Part II – Item 7. MD&A.” RISKS RELATED TO SEMPRA Operational and Structural Risks Sempra’s ability to pay dividends and meet its obligations largely depends on the performance of its subsidiaries and entities accounted for as equity method investments. We are a holding company and substantially all the assets that produce our earnings are owned by our subsidiaries or equity method investees, which are entities we do not control. SI Partners, which primarily constitutes our Sempra Infrastructure reportable segment, will be accounted for as an equity method investment subject to closing the planned sale of 45% of our equity interest, which we expect to occur in the second or third quarter of 2026. Our ability to pay dividends and meet our debt and other obligations largely depends on distributions from our subsidiaries and equity method investees, which in turn depend on their ability to execute their business strategies and generate cash flows in excess of their own expenditures, dividend payments to third-party owners (if any) and debt and other obligations. In addition, our subsidiaries and entities accounted for as equity method investments are all separate and distinct legal entities that are not obligated to pay dividends or make loans or distributions to us and could be precluded from doing so by legislation, regulation or contractual restrictions, in times of financial distress or in other circumstances. Any inability to access capital from our subsidiaries and equity method investees could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and/or prospects. Sempra’s rights to the assets of its subsidiaries and equity method investees are structurally subordinated to the claims of each entity’s trade and other creditors. When Sempra is a creditor of any such entity, its rights as a creditor are effectively subordinated to any security interest in the entity’s assets and any indebtedness of the entity senior to that held by Sempra. The principal terms of Sempra’s committed line of credit include the following: ▪ The facility has a syndicate of 23 lenders. No single lender has greater than a 6 % share in the facility. ▪ The facility provides for the issuance of $ 200 million of letters of credit. Subject to obtaining commitments from existing or new lenders and satisfaction of other specified conditions, Sempra has the right to increase its letter of credit commitment to up to $ 500 million. No letters of credit were outstanding at December 31, 2025. ▪ Borrowings bear interest at a benchmark rate plus a margin that varies with Sempra’s credit rating. ▪ Sempra must maintain a ratio of indebtedness to total capitalization (as defined in its credit facility) of no more than 65 % at the end of each quarter. credit_strengths.text: Sempra's regulated utility footprint in California and Texas provides stable, rate-base-driven cash flows, with operating income covering interest expense more than twice over. The current ratio above one signals adequate near-term liquidity, and the committed line of credit with no single lender above a modest share supports backup funding for commercial paper.

Operating cash flow remains substantial, exceeding four and a half billion, and the company retains access to a committed line of credit with available unused capacity. The planned sale of a minority stake in Sempra Infrastructure Partners and the Ecogas divestiture should generate meaningful proceeds, strengthening the balance sheet and funding growth without incremental leverage.

key_risks.text: Sempra is a holding company dependent on distributions from subsidiaries and equity method investees, which are structurally subordinated and not obligated to pay dividends. The planned sale of a forty-five percent interest in SI Partners will shift that segment to equity method accounting, potentially reducing consolidated cash flow and increasing reliance on external distributions.

The debt maturity profile includes a substantial current portion and a large short-term borrowing balance, while free cash flow is negative after heavy capital expenditure. The company must refinance or repay these obligations amid a highly leveraged capital structure, and the credit facility's indebtedness-to-capitalization covenant provides limited headroom if earnings decline.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage of roughly two and a quarter times is below the sector median, and net leverage near six times exceeds the median, indicating a highly leveraged profile. Operating cash flow covers only a modest fraction of debt, and free cash flow is negative after capital expenditure, so debt service depends on continued access to capital markets and refinancing.

The company faces significant maturities within the next twelve months and a large short-term borrowing balance, while cash on hand is minimal. Refinancing risk is mitigated by the committed line of credit and investment-grade access, but the negative free cash flow and high leverage leave little cushion if market conditions tighten or capital expenditure remains elevated.

overall_credit_view.text: Sempra's credit profile is characterized by stable regulated utility operations offset by high leverage and negative free cash flow. The indicative financial risk profile is highly leveraged, with leverage above the sector median and cash flow coverage below it. The planned asset sales and committed credit facility provide some flexibility, but the company remains sensitive to interest rates and regulatory outcomes.

Our forward-looking view is that leverage will remain elevated near current levels unless asset sale proceeds are applied to debt reduction or earnings grow sufficiently to improve coverage. The negative free cash flow and substantial capital expenditure program suggest ongoing external funding needs. We would monitor the completion of divestitures, regulatory decisions, and any deterioration in cash flow coverage as key credit drivers.

credit_strengths.text: Sempra於加州及德州的受規管公用事業版圖提供穩定、以費率基礎驅動的現金流，營運收入覆蓋利息支出超過兩倍。流動比率高於一，顯示短期流動性充足，而承諾信貸額度中並無任何單一貸款人佔比過高，為商業票據提供備用資金支持。
營運現金流仍然龐大，超過四十五億，且公司仍可動用承諾信貸額度中未使用的可用容量。計劃出售Sempra Infrastructure Partners少數權益及Ecogas剝離應可產生可觀收益，在不增加槓桿的情況下強化資產負債表並為增長提供資金。

key_risks.text: Sempra為控股公司，依賴附屬公司及權益法投資對象的分派，該等分派在結構上屬次級，且並無義務派付股息。計劃出售SI Partners百分之四十五權益將使該分部轉為權益法會計，可能減少合併現金流並增加對外部分派的依賴。
債務到期結構包括龐大的流動部分及大額短期借款結餘，而自由現金流在沉重資本開支後為負。公司須在高槓桿資本結構下為該等債務再融資或償還，而信貸融資的債務對資本化比率契約在盈利下跌時提供的空間有限。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率約為兩倍多，低於行業中位數，而淨槓桿接近六倍，高於中位數，顯示槓桿高企。營運現金流僅覆蓋債務的一小部分，且自由現金流在資本開支後為負，故償債依賴持續進入資本市場及再融資。
公司於未來十二個月內面臨重大到期債務及大額短期借款結餘，而手頭現金極少。再融資風險因承諾信貸額度及投資級別准入而有所緩解，但負自由現金流及高槓桿在市場環境收緊或資本開支維持高企時留下的緩衝極少。

overall_credit_view.text: Sempra的信貸狀況特徵為穩定的受規管公用事業營運，被高槓桿及負自由現金流所抵銷。指示性財務風險狀況為高槓桿，槓桿高於行業中位數而現金流覆蓋低於中位數。計劃中的資產出售及承諾信貸設施提供一定靈活性，但公司仍對利率及監管結果敏感。
我們的前瞻性觀點是，除非資產出售所得用於減債或盈利增長足以改善覆蓋，否則槓桿將維持於接近目前水平的高位。負自由現金流及龐大資本開支計劃顯示持續的外部資金需求。我們將監察剝離交易的完成、監管決定及現金流覆蓋的任何惡化，作為關鍵信貸驅動因素。
